title: Nodes get irregularly unuseable
body: We run OKD 4.14 with OVN and Istio ambient mode. Irregularly, istio-cni becomes non-ready, then ztunnel becomes non-ready, and the entire node becomes unreachable over the network: no SSH, debug session, or ping. The affected host has different ISTIO iptables/nftables rules from healthy nodes, including rules that look like workload redirection rules. Debug logging initially showed little and I could not reproduce it reliably. Later, immediately after enabling a customer namespace for ambient and adding a workload, ztunnel crashed while istio-cni survived; I captured the CNI log showing the workload's iptables restore commands before draining the node.

symptoms_visible: Irregularly, istio-cni becomes non-ready, then ztunnel becomes non-ready, and the node becomes completely unreachable: I cannot SSH, start a debug session, or ping it.
After enabling a customer namespace for ambient and adding a workload, ztunnel crashed again; the CNI log contained iptables restore commands immediately beforehand.
The ISTIO rules visible on an affected host differ from those on healthy nodes.
N0.label: N0 ambient nodes lose all network reachability

symptoms_visible: Five minutes after I upgraded to Istio 1.24.3, a random node developed the same network problem.
Repeatedly recreating pods in customer namespaces can make a node become unreachable, while similar testing in the bookinfo demo does not immediately trigger it.
N1_x.label: N1_x generic version upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: The node still becomes unreachable during pod recreation, and ztunnel becomes non-ready.
The affected applications are ordinary workloads such as MinIO, RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, and customer applications; there are also node DaemonSets for logging, storage, and OpenShift components.
N2.label: N2 detailed CNI evidence collected

symptoms_visible: I reproduced the node failure and found processes associated with the same pods reporting multiple network namespace inode values.
The affected shared node contains both mesh-enabled workloads and unrelated tenant workloads and DaemonSets.
N3.label: N3 multiple network namespaces demonstrated

symptoms_visible: After deploying the first candidate istio-cni image in the test environment, bookinfo traffic stopped, mesh-enabled nginx ingress pods became non-ready, and several nodes became unreachable after a few minutes.
The node failures occurred even without my chaos-testing.
N3_x.label: N3_x incorrectly published candidate image aftermath

symptoms_visible: After rebooting the affected nodes and deploying the corrected candidate image, the test environment remained healthy through chaos-testing and over the weekend.
istio-cni and ztunnel stayed stable and no nodes became unreachable.
N4.label: N4 corrected candidate verified in test environment

symptoms_visible: After deploying the official development build in development and then production, the environments remained stable and nodes no longer became unreachable.
N_terminal.label: terminal fixed in development and production

solution.intent: Treat the failure as an ambient implementation bug already addressed by later stability work and upgrade Istio to the first GA ambient release.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade from the current Istio installation to 1.24 because several ambient CNI and network-namespace bugs were fixed after 1.23.

edges.comment: Messages c1-c3, reporter's OKD cluster: a maintainer recommended upgrading because of later ambient fixes. The reporter installed 1.24.3, but the same node-level network failure recurred within minutes.

question_patterns: Can you enable debug logging and provide the complete istio-cni log around one failed workload, with a minute or two of context on each side?
Please choose one workload involved in a failure and share the corresponding CNI log interval.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled trace/debug logging and reproduced it. I uploaded the istio-cni log from about 9:08 to 9:14 PM; ztunnel became not ready at about 9:10 PM. I redacted customer data.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The CNI plugin is never invoked for any of the failed workloads, and the pod events only report that the container runtime could not create a network namespace.
I captured the same CNI activity with a five-minute buffer instead of two minutes.

question_patterns: Do any pods on these nodes use hostNetwork or elevated privileges?
What kinds of workloads are involved, and are the failing pods privileged?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The problematic pods are normal workloads such as MinIO, RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, and customer applications. We do have DaemonSets on every node for logging, storage, and OpenShift components, and some of those could use hostNetwork, but they are not part of the mesh. Our storage is attached over iSCSI.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every failing workload itself uses hostNetwork: true and is privileged.
The customer applications use different programming languages.

edges.comment: Messages c4-c11, reporter's cluster: maintainers requested complete CNI evidence and privilege/hostNetwork details. The reporter supplied the raw log interval and described the workloads without claiming a cause.

question_patterns: Can you run the supplied /proc script on an affected node and group its cgroup, network namespace, and command output by pod UID?
Please inspect processes for a specific pod and report the network namespace inode values associated with its cgroup.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced the issue and ran the script. With some awk help I found pods that have processes in multiple network namespaces, and I uploaded the complete multiplenetns.log. Not all of those pods are Istio-enabled because this is a shared multi-tenant node.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every process grouped under each pod UID reports exactly one identical non-host network namespace.
The same multiple-network-namespace pattern appears on another affected node with different pod UIDs.

edges.comment: Messages c12-c19, reporter's cluster: maintainers derived the need for a process/cgroup/netns dump from the CNI log. The reporter ran the requested script and personally stated that the output contained pods with multiple netns values; identifying CRI-O conmon and the host namespace remained engineer analysis.

solution.intent: Deploy the first hand-built istio-cni candidate intended to make network-namespace selection deterministic when more than one namespace is associated with a pod.
solution.concrete_example: Deploy the first candidate install-cni image in the test environment and exercise the ambient workloads.

edges.comment: Messages c19-c40, reporter's test environment: the reporter deployed the candidate offered by the maintainer. The tag expected to contain the host-netns protection was accidentally overwritten with an older build, and nodes again became unreachable. This is a real falsified attempt, not a failure of the later corrected build.

question_patterns: Please restart or otherwise clean the affected test nodes, deploy today's corrected image, and report whether the nodes remain reachable under the same workload test.
Can you retest the newly published image on clean nodes and tell us whether istio-cni, ztunnel, and node networking remain stable?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I rebooted the affected nodes, deployed the new image, and chaos-tested the test environment. No nodes became unreachable, istio-cni and ztunnel stayed stable, and the environment was still healthy when I checked over the weekend.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: On clean, rebooted nodes the newly published image still installs extra ISTIO rules on the host and the nodes become unreachable within minutes.
The environment stays healthy under normal workload churn, although I did not run the additional chaos loop.

edges.comment: Messages c37-c45, reporter's test environment: the maintainer acknowledged publishing the wrong image and supplied a corrected one. The reporter's deployment and stability observation are a pre-landing candidate-build measurement. Rebooting matters because rules left by the broken build persist across CNI upgrades.

solution.intent: Use an official Istio CNI build that excludes the host network namespace when resolving multiple namespaces associated with a CRI-O pod, repair nodes containing stale host-level Istio networking state, and verify stability before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Install the official development build containing the host-netns exclusion. Before evaluating it, restart affected nodes or carefully remove the stale Istio chains and related routing state written by the broken build. Then exercise ambient workloads and confirm that the nodes, istio-cni, and ztunnel remain reachable and ready.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers correlated the raw CNI and /proc output with CRI-O's process model: conmon can be grouped with the pod while remaining in the host netns, so choosing among multiple namespaces can cause workload iptables programming to run against the host. The accepted fix is to identify and exclude the host netns, not merely choose the oldest process.

edges.comment: Messages c44-c50, reporter's test, development, and production environments: maintainers explained that upgrading CNI does not remove host rules written earlier. After the change entered an official development build, the reporter deployed it in development and production and confirmed both remained stable.

solution.intent: Directly recognize the CRI-O multi-netns host-selection failure, deploy an official CNI build that excludes the host namespace, clean any persistent host networking state, and verify on the affected cluster.
solution.concrete_example: The host-level workload rules indicate that ambient CNI may be resolving a pod to the host namespace. Use an official build with host-netns exclusion, reboot or clean affected nodes first, and verify under workload churn that node networking and both CNI components stay healthy.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut gives credit for proposing the final accepted mechanism immediately from the host-level ISTIO rules and ambient failure pattern. It skips the thread's upgrade failure, process/netns collection, incorrect candidate image, and pre-landing verification.

edges.comment: Shortcut copy of the accepted answer, required because the first real recommendation was the falsified generic upgrade. It represents a correct first proposal for the reporter's same OKD cluster while still requiring verification before resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: on this CRI-O/OKD setup, processes associated with a pod can appear in both the pod and host network namespaces; Istio ambient CNI could select the host namespace and install workload interception rules on the host, making the node unreachable.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the unexpected host ISTIO rules, detailed CNI evidence, and the process/cgroup dump showing multiple network namespaces per pod.

The fix must use an Istio CNI build that identifies and excludes the host network namespace when selecting the pod namespace; merely choosing the oldest associated process is unsafe with CRI-O conmon.
Must not claim that a generic upgrade to the ambient GA release is sufficient: the reporter upgraded and reproduced the same failure.
Must not treat the first hand-built candidate as successful; the image actually deployed from that tag was stale and nodes again became unreachable.

Must account for persistent damage from a broken build: replacing istio-cni or restarting pods alone does not remove spurious host iptables or routing state, so affected nodes must be restarted or carefully cleaned before retesting.

Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing the host-netns exclusion on clean or repaired nodes, and only declare resolution after affected development or production environments remain stable.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Kubernetes and OpenShift platform operator who can manage Istio installations, inspect nftables/iptables, collect component logs, run node-level /proc scripts, test custom images, and operate test, development, and production clusters, but does not consider themself a network-stack specialist.
persona_hint.communication_style: Highly cooperative, candid, and persistent; supplies long logs and concrete deployment observations, asks for exact collection instructions, expresses uncertainty rather than overstating conclusions, and quickly tests proposed builds.
